variant_policy: Where a publisher offers a reduced edition, the reduced edition is taken and named: basic, base, simple, lite or slim. A reduced product is not a synonym for the full axiom set, and loading several of them does not reconstruct axioms their publishers omitted.

declared.note: The AE core ontology that represents this knowledge graph. Byte-identical to site/resources/ontology/ae_standalone_fixed_2026-09-10.owl, so the loader recognises it and skips it: ingestion already publishes the core to the graph/ontology named graph.

Biological process, molecular function and cellular component. The basic edition is acyclic and omits cross-aspect relationships; its versionIRI names go.owl, which is how the publisher labels the release, not a substitution of the full product.

Cross-species anatomy including nervous-system structures. The full edition, replacing the basic edition: it carries the axioms the basic product omits, which is what a part-of closure over anatomy needs.
Cell types including neurons and glia.
Provisional cell populations, for cell-atlas integration. No reduced edition is published.
Disease identifiers including neurological disease.
Human phenotypic abnormalities including neurological findings.
Chemical grounding. The lite edition carries the class hierarchy without chemical data properties.
Species. The slim subset is taken because the full taxonomy is far larger than anything this corpus references.
Behavioural processes and behavioural phenotypes.
Mental functioning.
Emotion. MFOEM is the Emotion Ontology; EMO is Enzyme Mechanism Ontology and is not this.
Mental disease.
Mammalian phenotype, including neural phenotypes in model organisms.
Drosophila anatomy, including nervous-system structures.
C. elegans anatomy, including its nervous system.
Zebrafish anatomy, including neural structures.
Xenopus anatomy, including neural structures.
Protein Ontology: neural markers, receptors and channels. 1.2 GB, no reduced edition published; the download needed curl -C - to resume after the connection was reset.

Neuroscience Information Framework Standard Ontology. BioPortal submission 27, released 2018-02-10, pinned because an acronym alone does not identify a release. Import-only root: 3.8 KB declaring one owl:imports. BioPortal's artifact and the SciCrunch upstream are both shells, so NIFSTD needs its modules resolved rather than one file fetched.

Neuron Phenotype Ontology. BioPortal submission 22, released 2026-03-19, pinned because an acronym alone does not identify a release. Neuron Phenotype Ontology. NPO is the NanoParticle Ontology and is a different resource.

import_shells.note: These files declare owl:imports and carry almost no axioms of their own. A single-file load does not resolve imports, so the graph holds the header and little else. Their content needs the publisher's merged release or the imports resolved deliberately.

files.mfomd.owl: 42 triples loaded; imports MF.owl, ogms.owl, MD-core.owl and MF-core.owl.

discovery_candidates.note: Discovered by enumerating the BioPortal registry, not taken from a list: the catalog refers to a JSON under discovery.additional_bioportal_candidates holding 61 acronyms, and that file is not in this project. Selection was by BioPortal category (Neurological_Disorder, Neurologic_Disease) or neuroscience vocabulary in the title, excluding everything already declared above. The catalog calls these candidates "intentionally not preapproved", so they are staged in trusted_ontologies/candidates/ and published under the graph prefix .../graph/candidates/ rather than .../graph/trusted/. Nothing here has passed a scope, licence or quality review.
discovery_candidates.method: BioPortal /ontologies enumerated (1288 records); 73 selected; each resolved to a pinned latest submission.
